correctness.rationale: With \(A=I_n\) and \(h\equiv0\), the source step has \(\delta_k=\chi/\gamma_k\). The Moreau gradient of \(\|\cdot\|_1\) is coordinatewise clipping. Each raw coordinate update lies between the current coordinate and zero, so projection is inactive and signs are invariant. A positive coordinate limit would eventually lose \(\gamma_k/\chi\) at every step, contradicting nonsummability. Coordinatewise telescoping then gives the exact accumulated \(\ell_1\) motion, and \(\|v\|_2\le\|v\|_1\) yields finite Euclidean length.

value.rationale: The identity-map \(\ell_1\) box model is a canonical separable nonsmooth benchmark closely aligned with the source paper’s own \(\ell_1\)-type example. The theorem gives a complete schedule result for this whole finite-dimensional model class, not a single parameter point: every base-admissible smoothing schedule has finite Euclidean length, with an exact accumulated \(\ell_1\)-motion invariant. This cleanly shows that the source’s general \(\beta>1/2\) threshold is a class-level proof condition rather than an algorithmic necessity on all natural nonsmooth instances.
